# SB-1011 Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-HP03  
Related documents: MM-P3-L3-HP03, SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-02

Hazard description
- Summary: An arc flash hazard was identified at the induction power cabinet serving the machining hydraulic forging press EQ-P3-L3-HP03. The hazard arises from energized conductors and exposed connections at the cabinet where fault currents can produce arc flashes with thermal and blast effects. Contributing factors include degraded connection integrity, wear in power distribution components, and improper access during maintenance and setup activities.
- Background and incident rationale: During a recent inspection and maintenance observation, personnel reported visible sparking and localized charring at a connector and noted intermittent interruption of control signals to the press. Follow-up inspection revealed physical evidence consistent with low-energy arcing that can escalate to arc flash if a carrying conductor faults or if energized tooling contacts exposed parts. The induction power cabinet is a point of concentrated energy delivery to the press heaters and associated power electronics, making even short-duration faults a potential source of severe injury and equipment damage.
- Potential consequences: Electrical burn, thermal injury, blast pressure injury, hearing damage, secondary trauma from being struck by ejected parts, and damage to critical production equipment and controls that could lead to extended downtime.

Affected equipment
- Primary: EQ-P3-L3-HP03 induction power cabinet and associated power distribution components supplying Machining hydraulic forging press #3.
- Secondary: Local control enclosures and downstream power spans that interface with the cabinet and press.
- Personnel: Maintenance electricians, press operators, troubleshooters, and contractors who access or work within the cabinet boundary or who can be within the vicinity during energized work.

Required controls
- Administrative controls
  - Access restriction: Only authorized personnel with assigned electrical safety training and access rights may enter the cabinet or perform work on energized components. Authorization must be recorded against the maintenance work order and retained per site document control practices.
  - Work planning: All maintenance and troubleshooting activity involving the induction power cabinet must follow documented safe work procedures and pre-job briefings. Reference and comply with SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-02 for method steps, lockout/tagout sequencing, and specific PPE requirements where those SOPs apply.
  - Permit documentation: For any work that cannot be performed de-energized, a written energized work justification and approved permit must be completed and attached to the maintenance task record. Permits must reference MM-P3-L3-HP03 where mechanical maintenance impacts electrical components, and must document hazard controls, boundary delineation, and required PPE.
  - Training: Personnel performing work on or near the induction power cabinet must complete recurrent electrical safety and arc flash awareness training as prescribed by site training governance; training completion must be recorded in personnel training records and associated with the work authorization.
- Engineering and physical controls
  - Connection integrity: Inspect and secure all power connections, bus bars, and terminations within the induction power cabinet. Torque critical fasteners per equipment data; note that the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. Use calibrated tools and document calibration status in the tool/inspection log.
  - Guarding and labeling: Ensure that the cabinet has secure mechanical barriers, interlocks, and clearly visible arc-flash warning labels at each access point. Maintain required clearances and pathways for safe egress and emergency response.
  - Equipment condition monitoring: Implement and log periodic visual and thermal inspections of high-energy connections and components. Trending of inspection findings should be used to identify degrading connections before failure.
  - Interlocks and remote isolation: Where practicable, use remote isolation and verify de-energization at the point of work. Where de-energization is not possible, use engineered barriers and remote handling tools to increase separation between personnel and energized parts.
- Personal protective equipment (PPE)
  - PPE selection must follow the applicable SOPs and site PPE matrices based on assessed incident energy or the absence of de-energization; selection rationale must be documented in the permit when energized work is approved.
  - PPE and clothing must be inspected before each use and records of inspections maintained in the PPE inventory log.

Examples and step rationale
- Example 1 — Planned maintenance: During scheduled replacement of a power contactor, the task is planned to be performed de-energized whenever possible. The maintenance planner references SOP-P3-L3-01 to complete lockout/tagout and uses a calibrated torque wrench to verify connection torques. The rationale is to minimize energized exposure and ensure mechanical integrity to prevent arcing upon re-energization.
- Example 2 — Emergency troubleshooting: If the press exhibits unexpected cycling and troubleshooting requires live measurement inside the cabinet, a written energized work permit is completed per SOP-P3-L3-02. Two-person rule applies: one person performs measurements while a second qualified person monitors and maintains communication. The rationale is to limit exposure time and provide immediate assistance in case of an incident.
- Tool usage: Calibrated torque tools must be used to achieve specified connection torque and must be included on the tool calibration roster cited in maintenance tasks. The torque value specified for the main ram bolt is provided to ensure correct clamp force and mitigate arc initiation from loose connections.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work orders: Attach completed checklists, lockout/tagout forms, and energized work permits to the annual maintenance record for EQ-P3-L3-HP03.
- Torque verification: Record each instance of torque verification for the main ram bolt and other critical connections in the press maintenance log and retention system. Include tool serial number and calibration status as part of the entry.
- Inspection logs: Maintain visual and thermal inspection records for the induction power cabinet in the electrical inspection folder. Include corrective actions and response dates.
- Training and authorization: Retain training completion certificates and authorization rosters for personnel authorized to work on the cabinet.
- Incident and near-miss reports: Document any anomalies, near-misses, or actual incidents involving the cabinet in the incident management system and reference MM-P3-L3-HP03 where mechanical aspects contributed.

Effective date
- Effective date: Implementation of the controls and recordkeeping described herein is required upon release of Rev E. All referenced SOPs and maintenance manuals must be consulted prior to performance of work: MM-P3-L3-HP03, SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-02.

Distribution and follow-up
- This bulletin must be distributed to plant management, maintenance supervision, electrical trades, local safety committee, and contractor supervision for P3, line P3-L3. Supervisors are responsible for ensuring awareness, updating local procedures to reflect these controls, and confirming completion of required training and record updates.
